text:
Utah had the puck, the shots and the faceoffs. Winnipeg had Gabriel Vilardi and Stuart Skinner, and that was enough for a 4-2 win.

The first period was a track meet: four goals in a little over nine minutes. Vilardi scored at 5:11 on a backhand, Andrew Peeke answered 67 seconds later, Vilardi struck again at 7:26 on a 4% chance, and Lawson Crouse tied it at 10:22. Morgan Barron's tip at 14:00 put the Jets ahead for good, and our win model counted it as the biggest swing of the night, 52% to 69%. Vilardi completed the hat trick into an empty net with seven seconds left.

What came in between was mostly Utah. The Mammoth outshot Winnipeg 36-15, took 64 shot attempts to 32, won 31 of 44 faceoffs and owned the second period, 1.03 expected goals to 0.24. They had the better even-strength chances, 2.13 to 1.76, and deserved to win 63% of the replays of this game's shots. The Jets managed 15 shots on goal in a home game and won anyway.

That is Skinner's work. He stopped 34 of 36, saved 0.55 goals more than expected and made his biggest save on Vincent Trocheck late in the third, a save that swung about a third of a win in our model. With Connor Hellebuyck traded to New Jersey in October, nights like this are how Winnipeg answers the question of who holds the net. Kyle Connor added two assists, two nights after Mark Scheifele became the franchise's all-time leading goal scorer.

For Utah, the loss lands on its new starter. Sebastian Cossa, who has taken the crease from Karel Vejmelka in what The Hockey News called a goaltending shakeup, allowed three goals on 14 shots, about 1.1 more than they deserved. One bad night on 14 shots says little about a goalie. It does sting when your team outshoots the opponent by 21.
headline: Vilardi's hat trick, Skinner's 34 saves sink Utah
